records.originalTitleAtApproval: Not with Eyeservice — faithful work when no one is watching
records.displayTitle: Who Is Watching When You Work Alone?
records.promoDescription: This lesson shows how Yahweh sees every room, and why faithful work in small, unseen tasks matters to Him more than being noticed by others. It also looks honestly at sloth, the value of rest, and how to judge others by their fruit rather than by assumptions.

visual.prompt: A content, focused Black woman in her thirties in a cobalt blue blouse works at a light oak desk in a bright home office with big windows, white shelves and lush green plants, writing in a planner beside a laptop with a soft, satisfied smile, nobody else in the room; clear daylight, fresh greens and blues.
visual.alt: A Black woman works contentedly at her desk in a bright, plant-filled home office.

records.originalTitleAtApproval: Give Me This Mountain — Strength Kept for the Second Half
records.displayTitle: Is Your Strongest Season Still Ahead of You?
records.promoDescription: At eighty-five, Caleb asked Yahweh for the hard hill country he had been promised decades earlier, and this lesson looks at what his request teaches about setting aside gifts, waiting well, and passing faith to the next generation. It also addresses the flat, worn-down feeling many people carry in the middle of life and the need to take it seriously.

visual.prompt: An energetic Black man in his eighties with a white beard, hiking boots and a red jacket stands on a green alpine trail pointing up toward a snow-capped summit with a determined smile, his grandson in his twenties beside him with a backpack, both faces clearly visible; meadow of wildflowers, clear blue sky, crisp daylight.
visual.alt: An older Black man in a red jacket points up a mountain trail beside his grandson under a blue sky.

records.originalTitleAtApproval: Whoso Removeth Stones — When One Small Fault Grounds the Flights
records.displayTitle: What Happens When One Small Part Stops the Whole System?
records.promoDescription: This lesson uses a reported air traffic outage, kept at its weight as unconfirmed, to teach three habits for changing any system: test before you change, stop when the readings disagree, and write the plan before the trouble comes. It also shows how Yahweh holds together what no system people build can hold.

visual.prompt: Bright modern airport control tower at midday, panoramic glass windows full of clear blue sky, sunlit runways and a white airliner taxiing outside. A confident Black woman engineer in her forties, crisp white shirt and lanyard, stands at a clean console checking a tablet before making a change, calm expressive face clearly visible, a younger Black male colleague in a sky-blue shirt beside her pointing at the tablet. Fresh natural daylight, vivid blues and whites, airy and hopeful.
visual.alt: A Black woman engineer and her colleague check a tablet in a bright airport control tower with planes on a sunlit runway outside.

records.originalTitleAtApproval: Wisdom Is Profitable to Direct — strategy, value, and the steward who points the resources
records.displayTitle: Working Harder Won't Fix a Dull Edge: Where Is Your Effort Pointing?
records.promoDescription: This lesson uses four strategy foundations from a finance newsletter (return on capital, long-term thinking, market attractiveness, and competitive advantage) and shows how the Word addressed each one first. It teaches that wise direction of our resources, starting with honoring Yahweh, matters more than simply adding more effort.

visual.prompt: Bright modern woodshop with big windows and clean light wood; a Black grandfather in his sixties in a sky-blue shirt guides his granddaughter, about ten, as she sharpens a chisel on a whetstone, both focused and smiling, faces clearly lit; green plants, natural daylight, tidy and inviting.
visual.alt: A Black grandfather teaches his granddaughter to sharpen a chisel in a bright woodshop.

records.originalTitleAtApproval: The Profit of the Earth Is for All — who gains when a company goes public
records.displayTitle: Does the Money From a Stock Sale Ever Reach the Field?
records.promoDescription: This lesson follows the money from one reported company stock sale and asks the question the Word asks: does the gain reach the field? It keeps each reported figure at its stated weight, weighs the risks, pledges, and conflicts involved, and points to Jesus as the pattern for how wealth is shared.

visual.prompt: Sunny green wheat field under a big blue sky with white clouds and a red barn in the distance; a Black woman farmer in her forties in a denim shirt and straw hat smiles while checking an abstract chart on a tablet, her teenage son beside her holding a basket of fresh vegetables; vivid greens, natural color.
visual.alt: A Black farmer checks a chart on a tablet beside her son in a sunny green field.

records.originalTitleAtApproval: A little leaven leaveneth the whole lump - a flaw in a shared runtime, and the watchman who finds every place it lives
records.displayTitle: Where Does a Hidden Flaw Live Inside the Tools You Already Run?
records.promoDescription: This lesson uses 1 Corinthians 5:6 and a real Java runtime security notice to show how a flaw can hide inside installed software, bundled apps, containers and appliances. It walks through how to find every copy, patch and restart it, and guard the system with a dated mitigation while the fix is pending.

visual.prompt: Vibrant, brightly lit modern data center aisle with white floors and glossy server racks glowing with electric cyan, teal and violet LED light, crisp bright overhead lighting. A focused Black woman security engineer in her thirties, natural hair, teal jacket, holds a tablet up to a rack, scanning it, her alert expression clearly lit, reflections of colorful light on her face. Dynamic depth, energetic cool color palette, high clarity, futuristic but real.
visual.alt: A Black woman security engineer scans a server rack with a tablet in a bright data center glowing with cyan and violet light.

records.originalTitleAtApproval: The camera and the image — Chris’s 4K eye
records.displayTitle: Why Does One Camera Decide What the Whole Room Sees?
records.promoDescription: This lesson explains why the camera is where every broadcast picture begins, and why problems there cannot be fixed later in the chain. It also shows why the main 4K feed is shared with both the Sanctuary screens and the Bishop's monitor, and why SDI cabling is used to carry it reliably.

visual.prompt: Bright modern church sanctuary during a daytime service, tall windows letting in natural light; a smiling Black woman camera operator in her thirties in a red polo shirt runs a professional broadcast camera on a tripod, the stage and congregation softly blurred behind her; clean whites, light wood, colorful accents.
visual.alt: A Black woman operates a broadcast camera in a bright church sanctuary during a daytime service.

records.originalTitleAtApproval: Name the Real Record and the Real Screen — The Trace That Runs Before Any Code
records.displayTitle: Would You Ship a Number You Couldn't Trace Back to Its Source?
records.promoDescription: This lesson teaches a four-step check developers run before building any user-facing screen: name the real data, confirm it connects end to end, observe the screen people actually use, and write the premise down first. It shows why a number that cannot be traced to a real record is worse than no number at all.

visual.prompt: Bright, airy modern software studio with floor-to-ceiling windows, city view, green plants and white desks in natural daylight. A smiling Black woman developer in her thirties in a coral top points at a large monitor showing a colorful abstract flow diagram of connected boxes and lines, while a young Black man in a mustard sweater leans in beside her, both engaged and expressive. Clean, modern, energetic, rich color accents of teal, coral and yellow.
visual.alt: A Black woman developer points at a colorful diagram on a monitor while a colleague leans in, in a bright, plant-filled studio.

records.originalTitleAtApproval: Two sets of weights in one bag
records.displayTitle: Is Your Property Math Honest in Both Directions?
records.promoDescription: This lesson shows why Yahweh forbids carrying two sets of weights, even when each property deal looks fair on its own. It gives you a way to set your buying and selling standards side by side, including cap rates, vacancy, fees, and repair reserves, so any hidden difference can be found and priced.

In the foreground a confident Black couple in their thirties in smart casual clothes stand on the sidewalk comparing details on a tablet with a friendly Black woman real estate agent in a navy blazer, all smiling and engaged, faces clearly visible. Crisp, professional, optimistic, natural color.
visual.alt: A Black couple and their real estate agent compare details on a tablet in front of two modern homes on a sunny street.

records.originalTitleAtApproval: When you buy a share, the company gets nothing — where shares actually come from
records.displayTitle: Why Would a Company Care About a Price It Never Gets Paid For?
records.promoDescription: Most share purchases move money between investors, not into the company, and this lesson explains the difference between the primary and secondary markets. It also covers why a business sells ownership at all, and the four reasons its leaders still watch the share price closely.

visual.prompt: Bright modern financial district plaza at midday, glass skyscrapers reflecting a clear blue sky, people walking in the sun. A confident Black woman investor in her forties in a tailored camel coat stands in the foreground looking at her phone, which shows an abstract green and blue line chart, a thoughtful half-smile on her clearly lit face. Clean, aspirational, modern, crisp daylight with rich blues and natural skin tones.
visual.alt: A Black woman investor checks a chart on her phone in a sunny financial district surrounded by glass towers.

records.originalTitleAtApproval: This I Recall to My Mind — time, memory, and what Yahweh does with a hard past
records.displayTitle: Can a Hard Past Be Rewritten, or Does Yahweh Make Something Else of It?
records.promoDescription: This lesson looks at time, memory, and choice from Scripture, showing that Yahweh knows the end from the beginning while our past does not reopen. It explores how recalling Yahweh's mercies reshapes a hard memory, and how Peter's worst night became a place of restoration.

visual.prompt: A Black grandmother in her seventies sits on a sunny front porch swing with a photo album and an open Bible on her lap, smiling warmly as her teenage granddaughter leans on her shoulder to look at the photos; green lawn, blue hydrangeas, clear blue sky.
visual.alt: A smiling Black grandmother shares a photo album and her Bible with her granddaughter on a sunny porch.

records.originalTitleAtApproval: Heavenly Cheat Codes: Life His Way — it is not cheating; it only looks like it because of all the winning
records.displayTitle: Is Life Really a Game Someone Else Has Rigged? What the Word Says About the Winning Code
records.promoDescription: This lesson explores why people who live by the Word of Yahweh often keep coming out ahead in ways others cannot explain, looking at the seed of Scripture, keeping it in heart and hands, and the examples of Joseph, Daniel, David, and Jesus. It also addresses the real deceiver in the story and how the victory is defined by Yahweh rather than by worldly success.

visual.prompt: Bright modern kitchen table beside a large window; a Black father in his thirties and his daughter about seven read an open Bible together, the girl pointing at a verse and laughing, the father smiling, faces clearly visible; white walls, green plants, cobalt and yellow accents, clear daylight.
visual.alt: A Black father and his young daughter laugh while reading the Bible at a bright kitchen table.

records.originalTitleAtApproval: It Doth Not Yet Appear What We Shall Be — how we were made, what was lost, and what Jesus restores
records.displayTitle: Were We Made Naked and Unashamed, and What Did Sin Really Take?
records.promoDescription: This lesson walks through what the Word says about how Yahweh made us very good, what sin brought in shame, fear and death, and why Jesus restores what was lost. It checks claims about Eden, Samson, Elijah and inherited guilt against the Scripture text itself.

visual.prompt: A sunny backyard garden gate: a Black father in his fifties warmly embraces his grown son in his twenties, the son's face showing relief and joy, an open white gate, blooming flowers and lush green lawn around them, clear blue sky; welcome and restoration, natural color.
visual.alt: A Black father embraces his grown son at a white garden gate on a sunny day.

records.originalTitleAtApproval: Count the Days — Numbers 1 to 7 from Creation
records.displayTitle: Can a Preschooler Count to Seven With Creation?
records.promoDescription: Children follow along as they count the six days Yahweh spent making the world and the seventh day He rested, using their fingers from one to seven. The lesson shows how the days of creation can be the very first numbers a young learner practices.

visual.prompt: Joyful, bright storybook-colored photograph: a cheerful Black girl about five years old in a sunny yellow dress sits in a lush green meadow full of colorful wildflowers, both hands raised happily as she counts on her fingers, big open smile. Butterflies, a soft rainbow and fluffy white clouds in a bright blue sky, bright midday sunshine. Vivid, playful, warm, full of wonder at creation.
visual.alt: A smiling Black girl in a yellow dress counts on her fingers in a sunny meadow of wildflowers under a rainbow.

records.originalTitleAtApproval: Adding and Taking Away — Loaves, Fishes, Baskets and Gideon’s Army
records.displayTitle: How Do Loaves, Fishes and a Small Army Teach Us to Add and Subtract?
records.promoDescription: This lesson walks through addition and subtraction using the loaves and fishes, the twelve baskets, Gideon's shrinking army, and a shepherd's one lost sheep. Learners write each equation and see how the Word counts what it has and says plainly what it did not count.

visual.prompt: Bright, cheerful classroom table by a large sunny window: a Black boy and a Black girl about eight years old laugh together as they count five golden bread rolls and two small colorful toy fish beside a wicker basket, with rainbow-colored wooden counting blocks lined up in front of them. A smiling Black woman teacher leans in to help. Vivid primary colors, soft daylight, joyful and educational.
visual.alt: Two Black children and their teacher laugh as they count bread rolls, toy fish and colorful blocks at a sunny classroom table.

records.originalTitleAtApproval: What Rent to Own Actually Is — The Model, and the Just Weight Laid Beside It
records.displayTitle: Can a Store Keep a Customer Without Holding Them? The Honest Math of Rent-to-Own
records.promoDescription: This lesson explains how rent-to-own works as a rental rather than a loan, and why the customer's freedom to return the item at any time means the store must earn every renewal through honor. It then weighs the industry's total cost, which the FTC has reported can run two to three times retail, against the Bible's call for just weights.

visual.prompt: Bright modern furniture and electronics store with big windows and sunlight; a friendly Black store manager in his forties in a navy polo hands a clear printed agreement to a young Black mother holding her toddler, both smiling, sofas and screens on display behind; clean, welcoming, colorful.
visual.alt: A Black store manager hands an agreement to a smiling young mother in a bright furniture store.

records.originalTitleAtApproval: Who should work, and who should not — the span of control, set by a father-in-law
records.displayTitle: Your Team Is Stalling Because You're Doing Everyone's Job: What Jethro Saw in Moses
records.promoDescription: Moses was judging Israel alone from morning until evening, and his father-in-law Jethro called it plainly not good, because no one person can carry that load. This lesson walks through the tiered structure and escalation rule Jethro gave, and the character-first criteria for choosing who should lead each layer.

records.originalTitleAtApproval: Read before you rule — learn on the real books
records.displayTitle: Why Would an Heir Be Given a Seat That Can't Change a Thing?
records.promoDescription: This lesson shows why a successor starts by learning to read the family's real financial books, using a read-only seat that reveals the truth without the power to change it yet. Drawing on David's charge to Solomon and Jesus' words on faithfulness in small things, it teaches knowing Yahweh first and then doing the work with care.

records.originalTitleAtApproval: Hearken → Blessings Overtake You
records.displayTitle: Why Would Blessings Hunt You Down Instead of the Other Way Around?
records.promoDescription: This lesson looks at Deuteronomy 28:1-2 and the pattern it lays out: diligent hearing and doing of Yahweh's commandments comes first, and the blessings follow. It shows why the believer's work is to engineer obedience rather than chase the blessing itself.

records.originalTitleAtApproval: The fatherless, the widow and the stranger
records.displayTitle: Does a Nation's Strength Show in Its Margins? Reading 1838 by Yahweh's Measure
records.promoDescription: This lesson proposes that Yahweh measures a nation not by its wealth or armies but by how it treats the fatherless, the widow and the stranger, people who have no leverage to force fair treatment. It applies that measure to the 1838–1839 Cherokee removal, asking who was left without protection and what the law did for each of them.

records.displayTitle: Why Does an AI Answer That Sounds Right Deserve the Most Doubt?
records.promoDescription: This lesson shows why a wrong answer that looks convincing is more dangerous than an obviously wrong one, and how to run AI output through a standard of truth before repeating it. It teaches a simple habit: check any factual claim against a real source first, then trust it.

It also explains how giving the model a role and audience sharpens its reply, and why this question-asking skill carries over to asking people good questions too.
